body: I updated the PR (and PR description) to also cover custom element reactions. That was the last big piece missing.

I run the `html-spec-review` skill on this PR and it found some problems (I still need to study / address it, but posting it here in case anybody is curious):
# Review — `async-context/html-pr` ([whatwg/html#13063](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/13063)) against its fork point on `main` Base `86190a4d` (merge-base with `main`) · head `524df481` · 20 commits · `source` only, 1085+/414−. Reviewed 2026-10-29. **How this was produced.** I read the full diff commit by commit and ran static checks on the base and the head, keeping only what the branch introduced. For each new parameter I grepped every call site with a multi-line-aware search. I compared the text against the proposal's web-integration documents at [`ff809754`](https://github.com/tc39/proposal-async-context/tree/ff809754b305600877acb2ace1628ea67cc07753), and re-checked [whatwg/webidl#1568](https://github.com/whatwg/webidl/pull/1568) at its current head `3188eabd`. Proposal documents cited below: - [`WEB-INTEGRATION.md`](https://github.com/tc39/proposal-async-context/blob/ff809754b305600877acb2ace1628ea67cc07753/WEB-INTEGRATION.md) (`WI`) - [`web-integration/html__events.md`](https://github.com/tc39/proposal-async-context/blob/ff809754b305600877acb2ace1628ea67cc07753/web-integration/html__events.md) (`EV`) - [`web-integration/html__custom-elements.md`](https://github.com/tc39/proposal-async-context/blob/ff809754b305600877acb2ace1628ea67cc07753/web-integration/html__custom-elements.md) (`CE`) **Locations.** Each finding names the algorithm, its anchor (`#id`) in a build of this branch, and a quoted step fragment. The `source:N` line given under **Fix at** is HEAD's line, for applying the edit. **Verdict.** The model is consistent across all 20 commits: capture synchronously, pass a required parameter or store a slot, fire `with` the mapping, and use « » for things the user agent decides. Every new parameter has all of its call sites updated: `seek` 8/8, *navigate an `iframe` or `frame`* 3/3, *iframe load event steps* 3/3, *process the linked resource* 2 overrides plus 1 caller. Every `load`/`error` fired at a `link` now carries a mapping. What remains: - **One unfinished placeholder.** A "TODO" note in *report an exception* (§1.1). - **Three blockers in the IDL integration.** Two depend on WebIDL; one is HTML's `EventHandler` callback context (§1.2). - **A cluster of focus/blur problems** (§2.1). - **A handful of smaller correctness and hygiene issues** in the later commits (§2.2–§3). --- ## 1. Blockers ### 1.1 🔴 Placeholder "TODO" note left in *report an exception* **Where:** *report an exception* (`#report-an-exception`), the step that sets *notHandled* by firing `error` at *global*: > TODO: Explain why we're manually fiddling with the context. **Fix at:** `source:121032` (from `f88a6c2a`). This is a `

` that contains an XXX ``, so it renders as a note with a TODO inside. It can't land as is. The same step has two smaller problems: - `source:121028` (112 columns) and `source:121032` (121 columns) are unwrapped. - The capture is inline (`CreateAsyncContextSnapshotObject(AsyncContextSnapshot())`). Everywhere else in the branch, the capture is its own step: `Let acMapping be AsyncContextSnapshot().` **Suggested note.** The rationale is already in [EV §8.1](https://github.com/tc39/proposal-async-context/blob/ff809754b305600877acb2ace1628ea67cc07753/web-integration/html__events.md#81---scripting) ("it must be explicitly overwritten and it would not always happen by default, as it can be triggered synchronously"): > *Report an exception* is often reached while the mapping of the code that threw is still > current, e.g. from within a timer callback or while executing a `script` element. The event is > fired in the empty mapping so that `error` listeners do not implicitly run in that context; it is > exposed explicitly through `uncaughtContext` instead. ### 1.2 🔴 The IDL integration doesn't work yet 1. **All four `[PropagatesAsyncContext]` annotations are no-ops.** This affects `toBlob`, `getAsString`, `queueMicrotask` and `requestAnimationFrame`. At `3188eabd`, whatwg/webidl#1568 doesn't add the attribute to WebIDL's closed list of extended attributes "applicable to types". So in `toBlob([PropagatesAsyncContext] BlobCallback _callback, …)` it attaches to the argument, not to the type, and the PR's capture step ("If the conversion is to an IDL type associated with the `[PropagatesAsyncContext]` extended attribute…") never fires. The fix belongs in WebIDL. 2. **`getAsString(FunctionStringCallback? _callback)` is nullable**, so it would fail independently even once (1) is fixed. #1568 has no step that carries an extended attribute from `T?` to `T`, and nullable conversion converts with the inner type. 3. **HTML's `EventHandler` callback context is still a bare settings object.** #1568 redefines the callback context as a pair (settings object, Async Context Mapping-or-null) and destructures it in *invoke* and *construct*. **Fix at:** `source:125825` (*getting the current value of the event handler*). The context should become (*settings object*, null). --- ## 2. Correctness ### 2.1 🟠 Focus/blur: one root cause, four symptoms **Where:** *focus update steps* (`#focus-update-steps`): the blur branch at `source:87768`, the focus branch at `source:87839`, and the `change` step (`#unfocus-causes-change-event`, `source:87741`). The intent is [WI "Cross-origin iframes"](https://github.com/tc39/proposal-async-context/blob/ff809754b305600877acb2ace1628ea67cc07753/WEB-INTEGRATION.md#cross-origin-iframes): `.focus()` on a cross-origin iframe's window must not carry the caller's context across. 1. **The guard is undefined without script on the stack.** It compares against the **current settings object**, i.e. the settings object of the current realm. When the focus update steps run without JS on the stack, there is no current realm. That happens when the user moves focus, in the event loop's focus fixup, in the unfocusing steps' fallback to the viewport, and in *flush autofocus candidates*. 2. **`change` is fired in the same per-entry loop as `blur`, without the guard.** So `crossOriginFrame.contentWindow.focus()` still runs a cross-origin `change` listener with the caller's mapping. 3. **Copy-paste bug.** The blur branch's Issue #3506 XXX says "If focus event target's relevant agent…" (`source:87783`); it should be blur event target. 4. **Markup.** - The blur branch's inner `

  • Fire a focus event … target.

    ` has no `
    • ` (`source:87777-87779`), unlike the focus branch. - Both branches leave a blank line before the closing `` (`source:87785`). - The prose "…then run the following steps with « ». Otherwise, run the following steps:" hangs one sub-list off two branches. That reads oddly and is part of why `change` was missed. **One fix for all four:** at the top of each per-entry loop body, compute the mapping once, then fire all events in that body with it. In the old-chain loop that's `change` and `blur`; in the new-chain loop, `focus`. > Let *acMapping* be « » if *entry*'s relevant agent is not the surrounding agent, or if there is a > current settings object and *entry*'s relevant settings object's origin is not same origin with > its origin; otherwise, `AsyncContextSnapshot()`. Then use "fire … with *acMapping*" (or "run the following step with *acMapping*") in place of the two hand-written branches. This removes the duplicated XXX notes (keep one per loop, with the right variable) and the unbalanced `
  • `. ### 2.2 🟠 Three early `error` paths in *prepare the script element* don't propagate **Where:** *prepare the script element* (`#prepare-the-script-element`), inside the `script-processing-src-prepare` step. Three paths queue an `error` event: an external `importmap`/`speculationrules`, an empty `src`, and an unparsable `src` (`source:69108`, `:69122`, `:69133`). All three return *before* "Set *el*'s execution Async Context Mapping to AsyncContextSnapshot()" (`source:69194`). So `s.src = ""` inside `v.run()` fires `error` in « », while `s.src = "404.js"` fires it with the mapping. [EV §4.12.1](https://github.com/tc39/proposal-async-context/blob/ff809754b305600877acb2ace1628ea67cc07753/web-integration/html__events.md#4121---the-script-element) asks for "the corresponding `load` and `error` events, *including* those fired while executing the script element". That wording implies the other `error` events, which are these three. **Fix:** capture into a local before `source:69100`, and fire those three with it. ### 2.3 🟠 Clearing the `Worker`/`SharedWorker` `error` entry on success happens off the owner's thread **Where:** - *run a worker* (`#run-a-worker`), the step "Associate *worker* with *worker global scope*", followed by "Clear AsyncContext for events with « "error" » given *worker*" (`source:137793-137797`). - The `SharedWorker()` constructor (`#dom-sharedworker`), "Associate *worker* with *workerGlobalScope*" (`source:138494-138497`). *Run a worker* says "Run the rest of these steps in that agent", so the success-path clear runs on the **worker's** agent. Meanwhile `worker` belongs to the **outside** realm. The `SharedWorker` branch runs on the shared worker manager's parallel queue. Both mutate the outside object's propagation map from another thread. The failure paths in the same commit get this right: they clear inside the task queued on *worker*'s relevant global. The notes argue the clear isn't observable, and that's probably true. Even so, mutating state from off the owning thread is something WHATWG reviewers will flag. **Fix:** queue a global task on *worker*'s relevant global object to do the clear. Alternatively, since it's unobservable, drop the success-path clears and keep the memory argument as a note at the IDL. Also: - Make the clear its own `
  • `, not a second `

    ` in the "Associate" step. - `source:137795-137797` wraps oddly: `«` ends a line, and `" So the `EventSource` constructor's Async Context Mapping reaches the first `open` or `error` > event and no later one *Reestablish the connection* is not a clearing point, as [EV §9.2](https://github.com/tc39/proposal-async-context/blob/ff809754b305600877acb2ace1628ea67cc07753/web-integration/html__events.md#92---server-sent-events) asks ("use that context to fire the `open` and `error` events queued by announce the connection, reestablish the connection, and fail the connection"). Take an initial connection that hits a network error and is reestablished. It fires one or more `error` events and then an `open`, all with the constructor's mapping. The note's first sentence is accurate ("only once the connection has either opened or failed permanently"); the second isn't. **Fix:** "…reaches every `open` and `error` event up to and including the first successful `open` or the permanent failure, and no later one." ### 2.6 🟡 ``: the abort-path `error` reads the slot inside the task **Where:** *start the `track` processing model* (`#start-the-track-processing-model`), the "If, while fetching is ongoing…" paragraph (`source:43333-43343`): "…fires an event named `error` at the `track` element with its track processing Async Context Mapping". That reads the slot **when the task runs**, not when the abort happens. A second `src` change in the same task overwrites the slot before the queued task runs, and the first abort's `error` then carries the second change's mapping. Arguably that's the right owner anyway. But everywhere else the branch captures before queuing, or (for ``) explains the late read in a note. **Fix:** either "let *abortAcMapping* be the element's track processing Async Context Mapping, and … fire … with *abortAcMapping*", or a sentence at `#track-processing-async-context-mapping` saying why a late read is fine. ### 2.7 🟡 Media: in-task slot reads with no justification at the slot definition **Where:** the *media data processing steps list* (`#media-data-processing-steps-list`). Six fires read "with its media loading Async Context Mapping" inside a task: `progress`/`suspend` at `source:39990`/`:39996`, `error` at `:40033`/`:40065`, `abort` at `:40090`, and `emptied` at `:40099`. Elsewhere, the same commit captures into `loadingAcMapping` before queuing. These reads are race-free because the *media element load algorithm* removes the element's pending tasks before the slot is rewritten. Nothing in the text says so, though, and a reader comparing the two styles will wonder. **Fix:** add one sentence to `#media-loading-async-context-mapping`. Something like: "It may be read from a task queued by the resource fetch algorithm, because the media element load algorithm removes those tasks before setting it again." ### 2.8 🟡 `loadingAcMapping` declared twice in the *resource selection algorithm* **Where:** `#concept-media-load-algorithm`. Step 1 has "Let *loadingAcMapping* be AsyncContextSnapshot(), and set the element's media loading Async Context Mapping…" (`source:39056`). The *Failed with attribute* step then has "…let *loadingAcMapping* be the element's media loading Async Context Mapping…" (`source:39183`). Same algorithm and same name, and the second read happens in parallel steps, which can't read element state. **Fix:** drop the second `let` and pass the step-1 variable. The other repeated `Let loadingAcMapping`/`playbackAcMapping` in the *resource fetch algorithm* and *ready states* sit in separate prose triggers that are mutually exclusive, and they bind the same value. They're fine. ### 2.9 🟡 The `
